title: Incident telemetry handoff + postmortem wizard
creator: Priya Shah
description: Build end-to-end incident tooling integration that attaches production telemetry (trace IDs, metric snapshots, log tails) to PagerDuty incidents and Slack incident threads, and surface an automated postmortem draft (postmortem wizard) populated with signal links and template prompts. Goal: reduce MTTI/MTTR by making context available to on-call and by accelerating post-incident analysis.
motivation: On-call engineers lose time hunting for traces and relevant logs after alerts. We already generate traces and dashboards but handoff to incident tools is manual. This work enables richer incident context in PD/Slack and semi-automated postmortem creation so teams can iterate on reliability faster.
acceptance_criteria: PagerDuty incidents created from Alerts must include a stable 'trace_link' and 'incident_snapshot' attachment with: representative trace IDs, top 3 alerting metrics with 5m/1h deltas, and a 500-line log tail URL.
Slack incident channels created by the Ops bot must display inline trace breadcrumbs and a collapsible metrics snapshot card with links to traces/dashboards.

Postmortem Wizard: clicking 'Create Postmortem Draft' from an incident pre-fills a Confluence draft with timeline skeleton, signal links, implicated services, and suggested RCA prompts; draft must be editable before publishing.
Feature toggles must exist (per-org) to enable PD enrichment, Slack enrichment, and postmortem draft generation independently.
No PII or secret values may be included in attachments; must pass security review and automated scrubber checks.
End-to-end tests and an observability dashboard must show success rate and latency for enrichment pipeline >= 95% over 24h during staged rollout.
Documentation: runbook templates and admin enablement docs published in Confluence and linked from Console settings.
Rate-limiting/backoff behavior in the PD/Slack enrichers must be implemented to handle API quotas without dropping enrichments silently.
progress_updates: 2026-02-15: Ticket created after reliability review. Initial scoping agreed: three parallel components (PD enrichment, Slack enrichment, postmortem generator).

2026-02-20: Design doc published: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Incident+Telemetry+Handoff+Design. Chosen approach: push enrichments from observability pipeline as attachments rather than altering alert payloads.

2026-02-25: Spike complete for PD attachments (trace_attachment_v2). Proof-of-concept attaches trace URL + metrics snapshot. POC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/1287 (WIP).

2026-03-01: Security review kickoff. Raised concerns about log-tail url access controls and retention; decided to mint short-lived signed URLs and require internal auth proxy. Action: infra ticket created ENG-23301.
2026-03-05: UX sync with PM/Design. Slack card wireframes approved. Decided to use block-kit cards with collapse for long payloads to reduce noise.

2026-03-08: Implementation started on PD side; created feature flag 'incident.telemetry.pd_enrich' and added integration tests for PD API error handling. Noted PD API rate limit of 200 req/min for large orgs — will implement 429 backoff queue.

2026-03-12: First internal canary run for a subset of alerts in staging. 88% success rate due to transient PD 429s; backoff strategy updated and circuit-breaker added. Current blockers: missing signed URL infra and final PR review.
blockers: Signed URL infra for log-tail snapshots (ENG-23301) must land before production rollout.
PagerDuty OAuth scopes require enterprise admin approval for some customer orgs; need PM/Legal to coordinate.
Conformance tests for telemetry scrubber (PII removal) need to be added to CI; security reviewer requested rigorous test cases.
Rate limit handling needs tuning for orgs that generate large numbers of alerts simultaneously.
decisions: Attach telemetry as separate incident attachments (attachments API) rather than modifying original alert payloads to preserve backwards compatibility and prevent breaking existing parsers.
Use short-lived signed URLs for large log archives to avoid embedding long payloads in PD/Slack and to satisfy retention policies.
Postmortem Wizard will generate drafts in Confluence instead of auto-publishing to ensure human review and avoid accidental leakage.
Start with read-only PD/Slack enrichment (links + summaries) for GA; consider experimental inline snippets after monitoring developer feedback.
risks_mitigation: PII risk: implement scrubber with allowlist/denylist for fields and add automated test suite that runs sample incidents through the scrubber.

API quota risk: implement prioritized queue and backoff with exponential retry and a durable tombstone if enrichment ultimately fails, and surface telemetry in Console so ops know enrichment failures.
Operational risk: feature toggles at org-level and rollout via canary groups to limit blast radius.
Security risk: security review and penetration test for signed URL service before prod rollout.
qa_plan: Unit tests for attachment serializer and scrubber
Integration tests hitting PD sandbox with mocked rate limits
End-to-end staging canary that exercises: alert -> enrichment -> PD incident -> Confluence draft
Manual verification checklist for on-call to validate trace links and metrics snapshot correctness
next_steps: Finish signed URL infra (ENG-23301) and add auth proxy tests
Complete PR reviews and merge PD enrichment branch
Roll out PD enrichment feature flag to 10% of orgs in staging and monitor enrichment success rate in the new telemetry dashboard
Implement additional scrubber test cases requested by Security and re-request review
Alpha launch Slack card enrichment for internal SRE team and gather feedback for iteration
notes: We intentionally avoid attaching raw log snippets to PD because some customers process logs with external sinks; instead we provide an authenticated log-tail URL and a 3-line excerpt in the attachment summary.
Consider future work: automatic prioritization of incidents for postmortem generation based on customer impact and alert noise score.
Estimate may be revised if signed URL infra requires additional compliance controls (HSM/KMS changes).
